title: Disney agrees to hire the majority of Character.AI’s workforce
abstract: After chatbot startup Character.AI filed for bankruptcy earlier this week, many of its employees will have the opportunity to take jobs at Disney. Character.AI’s former CEO Karandeep Anand recently became the entertainment giant’s first CTO , and the startup previously said that Disney had agreed to acquire some of its assets for $20 million. A legal filing spotted by Bloomberg revealed more details about the agreement between Character.AI and Disney, with Disney agreeing to make employment offers to at least 60 Character.AI employees — the majority of the workforce — paying them an estimated $60 million in annual compensation. The filing also says that the “vast majority” of Character.AI employees who were offered jobs at Disney accepted them. However, this is a stalking horse bid, so another company could come forward with a higher offer. The filing says that despite its “large and engaged user base,” Character.AI has been hobbled by high costs and “potential litigation-related liabilities and regulatory engagement.” (The company was sued by the mother of a 14-year-old boy who said her son became obsessed with one of Character.AI’s chatbots before committing suicide; it also faces government investigations over child safety concerns .)

title: Meta removes language that raised scraping and AI training concerns
abstract: Meta recently updated its commercial terms of use, declaring that the company can “use any content from [a business account’s] domains, web pages, or URLs to provide, develop, improve, research, train, and maintain the integrity of” Meta products and services. According to legal experts interviewed by Nieman Lab , this looked like a “remarkable provision” that could give Meta permission to scrape the website of any publisher with a Meta business account and use the content to train the company’s AI models. (While Meta defeated a high-profile lawsuit over alleged copyright infringement last year, other cases against AI companies, including Meta, continue.) However, a Meta spokesperson insisted that the updated terms did not reflect a change in the way Meta crawls the web. And now, The Verge reports that the provision has been removed. “We’ve heard you and want to clarify: the crawling terms we consolidated only applied to our ads and business products, and we’ve clarified that in the terms themselves,” the company said in a statement. “It does not change how Meta uses web crawlers.”

title: Anthropic says its workforce has become less junior and is spending more time in meetings
abstract: The composition of Anthropic’s workforce and the type of work getting done have changed significantly in the past year, according to a report that the AI company published on Friday. Anthropic argues that its own workplace trends could be indicators of “how AI will shift work organization, hiring, and labor demand across the economy,” especially since the company “has thoroughly molded its workflows around AI.” But even if other organizations never embrace AI as thoroughly or in the exact same way as Anthropic, the report offers an intriguing glimpse at how the company currently operates. Notably, Anthropic is making fewer junior hires, with the proportion of junior-level employees in technical departments falling from 21% to 14% since early 2025, and the proportion of junior technical hires falling even more sharply, from 27% to 9%. Anthropic also says that technical teams now represent a smaller share of the overall workforce, falling from 61% to 56% — a trend that it attributes to “natural expansion of business functions as the company scales,” as well as “coding tools increasingly allowing non-technical employees to make software themselves.” One employee reportedly described an “eternal pressure at Anthropic to move as fast as possible and use Claude for everything.” In an April 2026 survey, 27% of employees said they had become more productive because of Claude and 20% said their job had shifted “from actually doing work to managing Claudes”; apparently one engineered compared this to babysitting: “When you are babysitting, every child brings to you concerns with an equal demand for your attention and the various [Claudes] also do that.” In fact, the report suggests “human attention and judgement” are becoming a “bottleneck” for productivity, as Claude produces a “deluge” of text that needs to be read and organized. Unsurprisingly, the report argues that AI adoption has made the company more productive, as indicated by “more code per person, closing more sales per rep, and processing more contracts.” The company acknowledges that “more code does not necessarily mean better code or business impact,” but it also hasn’t found any indications that code quality is declining. The report says that based on calendar data, meeting time per employee is up 20% compared to a year ago, and it’s up 16% for technical contributors. The company attributes this to the importance of “human trust and accountability,” with employees repeatedly describing “face-to-face coordination as indispensable.”

title: TinyFish Makes Search Free: What It Really Costs an AI Agent to Read the Web
abstract: An AI agent that reads the web pays 2 kinds of cost. The first is the retrieval charge: what a search or fetch API bills per request. The second is model processing: content passed from retrieved pages into an AI model consumes tokens, while reasoning and generated responses add further costs. TinyFish , a web infrastructure company for AI agents, argues that teams budget for the model and underestimate how much retrieved content drives it. This article walks through the token math, the context-window impact, and what the Artificial Analysis Search API leaderboard does and does not show. Search and fetch APIs usually bill per request or per page. Whatever they return then enters the model’s context and is billed as input tokens. Reasoning and output tokens come on top. Enterprises now route each task to the cheapest capable model, a trend underlined when Stripe agreed to acquire OpenRouter , a gateway spanning 400+ models from 80+ providers. Routing lowers the price per token. It does not change how many tokens a retrieved page contains. Free Search and Fetch remove TinyFish’s retrieval charge within its limits. The downstream model still incurs inference costs. That is why the size of each returned page matters. TinyFish ran a fetch quality evaluation on June 2, 2026, across 45 URLs and 5 providers on default settings. For one Daily Mail article with a body of roughly 4,300 characters, the providers returned: *Marktechpost calculation: ~4 characters per token and an illustrative input price of $1 per 1M tokens. Input processing only; excludes retrieval charges, reasoning and output. Real counts vary by tokenizer. Character counts from TinyFish’s evaluation. In this example, Firecrawl returned approximately 36 times as many characters as TinyFish. Parallel also returned only an excerpt rather than the complete article, so its smaller output is not directly comparable to the full-page extractions. While this illustrates how extraction output size can affect token consumption, the difference comes from a single webpage and should not be generalized across all websites. Those percentages are not used for this individual page comparison because outputs above 30,000 characters were truncated before judging. Assume every extracted character goes into the same context, with no filtering, truncation or summarization. A page containing approximately 42,774 tokens would consume about one-third of a 128K-token context window. Three such pages would require approximately 128,322 tokens, leaving little or no room for system instructions, conversation history, or the agent’s response. Agent loops also resend context. Artificial Analysis notes that each turn resends the full conversation, with earlier input billed at the model’s cached-input price. Caching lowers the cost of rereading a noisy page. It does not remove it, and the page still occupies the window. In that TinyFish internal evaluation, a result counted as covered only with at least 1,000 characters and a judged signal ratio above 30%. Coverage was TinyFish 93%, Tavily 80%, Exa 73%, Firecrawl 62% and Parallel 58%. Among usable results only, median signal was 90.5% for TinyFish and 89.7% for Exa. TinyFish ran the test on itself, the sample is 45 URLs, and news pages drove most of the gap. TinyFish frames search as one operation inside execution, like DNS or storage for ordinary software. An agent booking, comparing or filling out a form should care whether the job got done, not which search system found the page. TinyFish attributes its free retrieval pricing to three aspects of its infrastructure: TinyFish charges separately for Agent and Browser usage, while Search and Fetch remain free within their published limits. Per the pricing page , Search is free at 30 requests per minute and 500 per hour. Fetch is free at 150 URLs per minute and 1,000 per day. Both keep working at a $0 Wallet balance. Agent costs $0.016 per step with 2 concurrent runs, and Browser costs $0.002 per minute with 5 sessions. New accounts get $8 in Wallet funds. Artificial Analysis holds the answer model fixed (GPT-5.6 Luna, medium) and changes only the search provider. Model cost covers input, cached, reasoning and output tokens. Differences between providers reflect returned payloads, how many searches the model runs and how much it reasons. On the Sep 28, 2026 snapshot, model cost ranges from $8.04 to $21.65 per 1,000 tasks across the 12 displayed configurations. These come from 26 products across 13 providers. TinyFish posts $0 for search plus $9.30 for the model, the lowest displayed total. The trade-offs: TinyFish recorded a Search Index score of 71, the lowest among the displayed configurations, and a DeepSearchQA F1 of 67. Its benchmark time was approximately 59 seconds per task, combining estimated model processing time and measured search time rather than representing API latency alone. Because Artificial Analysis uses its own shared extraction layer, the results do not directly measure TinyFish Fetch. Similarly, benchmark costs per 1,000 tasks should not be confused with API prices per 1,000 requests, since a single task may involve multiple searches. The table covers 3 selected competitors that appear in both the Artificial Analysis leaderboard and TinyFish’s fetch test. **Browser operation and research tasks are different capabilities, so these prices are not directly comparable. Pricing checked Oct 7, 2026: TinyFish , Exa , Firecrawl , Parallel . Benchmark data: Artificial Analysis (Sep 28, 2026) and its methodology . Coverage: TinyFish internal evaluation (June 2026) , a single-vendor test separate from the third-party benchmark. Thanks to the Tinyfish team for the thought leadership / resources for this article. title: Google Open-Sources Harness2, a Recursive Agent Harnessing Framework
abstract: Google Cloud AI Research has open-sourced Harness² . It is a recursive agent harnessing framework that improves the code and files around a frozen model. For developers, the pitch is simple. Your agent may get better without a better model. Harness² is a plug-and-play framework from Google Research that refines an agent’s harness during deployment. A harness is everything around the model: prompts, tools, memory, skills and orchestration . Harnessing is the process of optimizing that system. Model weights never change. The target setting is the open world. Tasks arrive unseen, and no verifier says whether an answer is right. The research team argues that most self-improvement methods assume labels or test cases. Harness² is built to work without them. Harness² exposes 8 editable components , each mounted as a file: They cover context construction, the tool interface, delegation and behavior inside the tool loop. The layout extends the 7-file split from earlier Agentic Harness Engineering work by 1 component. The framework runs two linked levels of recursion : The budget k scales the search. Parallel mode probes k invariant and k domain candidates, then makes k compositions. Sequential mode chains k refinement steps. The research team tested 3 professional benchmarks: WorkBuddy-Bench , JobBench and Harvey’s LAB . Executors were Gemini 3.5 Flash and GLM-5 under OpenCode and Codex. The default editor was Claude Opus 4.8. Results are means over 3 runs. Source: Harness² paper, Tables 1 and 2 . Weaker executors gained more. After 1 step, GLM-5 beat base Gemini 3.5 Flash on WorkBuddy-Bench. Parallel recursion at k=5 lifted Gemini under OpenCode to 80.8 on WorkBuddy . On WorkBuddy-Bench, 3 of 4 setups also used fewer steps per task. Gemini under OpenCode fell from 25.4 to 21.9. *Scores as measured in the Harness² paper ; the other methods did not report these benchmarks themselves. The README targets Linux, Python 3.12 and uv. A local demo runs both recursion modes without model credentials: Model-backed runs need Node.js 20+, the Google Cloud CLI and a Vertex AI project. LAB needs Pandoc and Poppler. WorkBuddy-Bench needs Docker. Executors are OpenCode by default, or Codex with --substrate cx . Check out the Paper , GitHub Repo , Paper and Project Page . title: How to Make Zero-Training Tabular Predictions with NVIDIA Structured Data Models
abstract: In this tutorial, we implement Structured Data Models , NVIDIA’s new library that puts several pretrained foundation models for tables behind one PyTorch interface, and use it to make predictions without training. The library wraps TabICLv2 and KumoTabular for single tables and KumoRelational for whole relational databases, and each of them answers by in-context learning: we hand the model a set of labeled rows and the rows we want predicted, and it returns probabilities or a full predictive distribution in one forward pass. We start with the library’s typed table tensors, compare the two tabular models against trained scikit-learn baselines, reuse an encoded context across many queries, read calibrated prediction intervals off a regression, and scale to twenty classes. We then look at the places where the defaults quietly do the wrong thing: a preprocessing recipe that drops timestamp and text columns and an explainer with two traps in it, before building a small three-table shop database and predicting customer activity from it directly, including the one argument that separates an honest relational model from a leaky one. Check out the Full CODES here . We install Structured Data Models from the GitHub repository, pinned to the commit this notebook was verified against, since the package on PyPI is only a placeholder. The relational sampler also needs pyg-lib, and that is where the first trap lies. pyg-lib wheels are published per minor PyTorch release, on pages named like torch-2.14.0+cpu, but the library’s own ImportError builds the URL from the exact patch version, torch-2.14.1+cpu, which is an empty page, so following its advice fails. We build the index URL from the major and minor version instead. We run everything on the CPU, which is the path verified end to end here, and print the models the library exposes together with their checkpoint sizes and licenses; the two Google models it also wraps, TabFM and TimesFM 3, are large and non-commercial and are left out. Check out the Full CODES here . Everything in the library flows through TableTensor, a PyTorch tensor subclass that keeps one typed block per semantic type: numerical, categorical, datetime, text and id. infer_stypes decides the types, and with its defaults it gets two things wrong on a realistic support-ticket frame: the free-text comment becomes a categorical with four hundred levels and the ticket id becomes a number, so both would reach a model as features. Passing text and id inference flags fixes that. The round trip back to pandas preserves every value, missing ones included, but not every dtype: numbers return as float32 because the numerical block is a single float tensor, nullable integers become floats with NaN, and categorical strings return as a pandas category. On pandas 2.x the string columns print as object rather than str and the timestamp goes in at nanosecond resolution; the same values come back either way. One more trap is worth knowing before you load a real event log: the library stores datetimes as integer microseconds, and Arrow refuses any cast that would drop a digit. A nanosecond column of whole seconds converts fine, but a single value with nanosecond digits fails the whole column, so we floor timestamps to microseconds first. Check out the Full CODES here . The tabular models take labelled context rows and unlabelled query rows and return a TableTensor with one probability column per class, named by label, so there is no fit step and no hyperparameters. On the breast cancer dataset, with three hundred labelled rows and two hundred and sixty-nine to predict, TabICLv2 and KumoTabular reach 0.970 accuracy and AUCs of 0.996 and 0.995 with no training, against 0.970 and 0.993 for a logistic regression and 0.967 and 0.992 for gradient boosting, both fitted on the same three hundred rows. num_estimators sets how many differently preprocessed views of the data the model averages over, which is the library’s built-in ensembling. Calling the model directly re-encodes the context on every call. When the same labelled rows will answer many batches of queries, fit encodes the context once into a key and value cache and predict then runs only the query rows; clear frees the cache. Nothing is learned in fit, which here means remember these examples. Answering five batches of thirty rows against the same four hundred context rows finished several times faster this way on our CPU, and once the context was cached, each further batch cost a small fraction of a full forward pass. The exact ratio depends on the machine, which is why the cell measures it rather than assuming it. For regression, the model does not return a single number. It returns 999 quantiles per query row, a full predictive distribution read off one forward pass. On the diabetes dataset with three hundred labelled rows, the median of that distribution has an RMSE of 53.6, slightly better than RidgeCV at 54.3 and clearly better than gradient boosting at 64.7, both trained on the same rows. The more useful property is calibration: the interval between the 10th and 90th percentiles contains 81.0 percent of the held-out targets and the 5th to 95th percentile interval 91.5 percent, close to their nominal 80 and 90 percent, while the 50 percent band runs somewhat narrow at 43.7 percent. The pretrained classification head has a fixed number of class slots, and the library handles problems with more classes than that through error-correcting output codes, splitting the problem into smaller coded subproblems and recombining the log-probabilities. The caller never sees this: on a balanced twenty-class synthetic problem with thirty labelled rows per class, TabICLv2 returns twenty probability columns and reaches 0.760 accuracy in a single forward pass, against 0.615 for gradient boosting trained on the same rows. Preprocessing in the library is a Recipe of composable processors, and the default TabICLv2 recipe dispatches on semantic type with branches only for categorical and numerical columns. Timestamp and text columns therefore never become features. On support tickets whose escalation depends on when they were opened and on words such as refund, the default recipe scores an AUC of 0.525, close to chance. The library does emit a RuntimeWarning naming the ignored column types. Still, it is a warn-once: it fires the first time and is suppressed for the rest of the process, so every later model in the same notebook or service drops those columns in silence. Prepending two processors fixes it: AddCalendarFields turns the timestamp into cyclic hour and weekday features, lifting the AUC to 0.634, and TFIDF adds the comment’s terms, lifting it to 0.789. The library’s GradientExplainer returns the gradient of a chosen output with respect to the preprocessed query inputs, and we test it on synthetic data where only three of eight features matter, with known signs. It has two traps, both visible only by looking at what the output function receives. First, the function is called once per estimator and each call overwrites the previous result, so with four estimators an output function that is live only on the first call yields an all-zero explanation, and the explanation you get is only the last estimator’s. Second, each estimator’s raw output has its own class order, because the default recipe shuffles class labels per estimator. Explaining with a single estimator across six seeds, selecting the probability of class one by column position flips the sign of every feature on the two seeds whose order is reversed, while selecting it by column name gives the right sign on all six, and averaging over the seeds recovers the three real features with the noise features near zero. KumoRelational takes a relational database instead of a single table.

title: Meet Voxel51 3.0: A Unified Multimodal Data Platform for Physical AI
abstract: Voxel51 has released Voxel51 3.0 , a very important update to its data platform. Voxel51 3.0 is an end-to-end multimodal data platform that puts search, curation, annotation and evaluation in one system. It targets teams training models on sensor data from robots, vehicles and factories. The release adds Voxel51 Agent, a data provenance layer and free self-service access . Voxel51 3.0 expands the platform beyond its roots in visual data with 3 core additions. Supported modalities include MCAP, images, video, 3D point clouds, meshes, DICOM, NIfTI, geospatial data and audio. Voxel51 Search is a persistent hybrid index. It indexes datasets and computes embeddings automatically, so search works from day 1. Semantic retrieval finds visually or semantically similar moments, even without shared labels. Lexical and structured queries handle exact terms, timestamps, sensor fields and metadata. Embeddings and structured fields stay in native form and are combined at retrieval time. Vector retrieval runs on LanceDB. It supports vector, scalar and full-text indexes, and separates storage from compute. Teams choose what to embed, which model and compute to use, and when. Incremental updates avoid full rebuilds when samples arrive or schemas change. Voxel51 Agent chains search, curation, annotation and evaluation into repeatable workflows. The agent can also write code to build custom plugins. All workflows inherit the organization’s permissions and governance controls. Voxel51 3.0 adds 4 provenance layers : Events flow through fiftyone-mq for job scheduling and Activity Core for event tracking. Yes. The platform is model-agnostic across embeddings, auto-labeling, inference and evaluation. A team can bootstrap with a foundation model, then swap in its own domain model. Voxel51 cites its 2026 State of Physical AI survey . 58% of “exceptional” teams spend more than half their project time on data work. Only 21% of struggling teams do the same. This is vendor-run research, so read it as directional. Encord’s sensor-stream support is stated in its Series C release . Prices verified October 17, 2026. title: Meet Kyutai REKI: The 2.4B VLA Model Bringing Efficient Memory to Robot Manipulation
abstract: Kyutai, with Inria and École des Ponts, has released REKI , a 2.4B vision-language-action model (VLA) for robot manipulation. The REKI vision-language-action model is pretrained only on public data. It also carries a cheap memory of its recent past. On three out-of-distribution benchmarks, only models about twice its size beat it. All weights are live on Hugging Face today. REKI is a vision-language-action model from Kyutai that maps camera views and an instruction to robot actions. It pairs a Qwen3.5-2B backbone with a 200M-parameter action expert. The expert generates action chunks by flow matching, integrated in 10 Euler steps. Robot state and flow time enter through adaptive RMSNorm. Each robot state layout gets its own small state MLP. Most VLAs act on the current frame alone. Prior memory methods feed past frames to the VLM, unroll training, or add modules. Each option adds cost. REKI places memory inside the action expert instead. Before each frame’s action tokens sit 32 learned register tokens . They cross-attend the encoded prompt and views of that frame. They also self-attend the registers of earlier frames. Registers never read action tokens. So they depend only on observations, not flow time or robot state. They are computed once per frame and cached in a rolling window. The cost is small, per the project page : Memory also fixes a failure mode. Without it, arms often oscillate between 2 poses. On RoboTwin, oscillating episodes fall from 18.6% to 4.1% with memory. Kyutai attributes this to perceptual aliasing. REKI is pretrained once, then finetuned separately per benchmark. Scores below come from the model card and project page. Pretraining helps most out of distribution. It adds 13.8 points on Clean2Rand and 30.3 under clutter. Memory adds 1.5 points on LIBERO-Plus and 5.4 on RoboCasa365. Notes: Clean2Rand means are computed from the 6 conditions in Table 5 of the Qwen-RobotManip report . The Qwen report lists π0.5 at 84.4 on LIBERO-Plus. The mixture holds 1.0B frames plus 12.2M vision-language samples. Real-robot teleoperation provides 639.8M frames, simulation 193.9M and egocentric human video 170.9M. Sources include DROID, BridgeData V2, AgiBot World, EgoDex and EgoVerse. Pretraining ran 200,000 steps on 32 H100 GPUs. Kyutai keeps each dataset’s native control convention rather than remapping actions. Six checkpoints are listed: the pretrained base plus finetunes for LIBERO, RoboTwin (2 variants), RoboCasa365 and RoboCasa-GR1. Real-robot deployment uses the LeRobot async-inference gRPC protocol. On a UR5 arm, REKI was finetuned for 3k steps (1 hour) on 50 demonstrations per task. Check out the Paper , Project Page , Model Weights and GitHub Repo . title: Investing in the public benefit
abstract: Announcements Investing in the public benefit Oct 18, 2026 Today, we’re committing a portion of Anthropic’s shares to the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, a new entity with a structure that increases the stake as the company grows. Subject to stockholder approval, 5% of Anthropic’s shares will be committed today, with an additional 2% added at the board’s discretion for every 50% increase in the company’s value above a set baseline. As a public benefit corporation, most of our work in pursuit of our mission takes place inside the company: research relevant to AI safety and interpretability; applied biomedical research; discounts on Claude for nonprofits and scientific institutions. These activities have both a public benefit component and for-profit value, so we house them directly in the company. The Anthropic Public Benefit Fund will have increased flexibility and scale, enabling us to pursue our mission in new ways: for example, we might explore large donations to traditional nonprofits or direct distributions to specific populations. One example is labor market impacts. AI may generate enormous economic value, but it could also cause instability for many workers. Anthropic has already committed $200 million to studying and addressing this issue, but given the pace of AI progress, bolder approaches may be needed. The Fund will have the versatility to pursue them. We’re establishing the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund as a wholly-owned LLC—rather than a 501(c)(3) or other format—to give adjustability between different forms of giving. None of the Anthropic equity held by the LLC will be used for lobbying or political giving, in the US or abroad. Because of the way the Fund is structured, the more Anthropic grows, the larger the share of the company that can be dedicated expressly to the public good. It is common practice for tech companies to offer escalating compensation awards to their executives. We are instead directing that equity to the public benefit. This builds on commitments our co-founders and employees have already made. When Anthropic was founded, our co-founders pledged to donate 80% of their equity holdings, and since founding we have also operated an equity donation match program that allows employees to pledge equity which Anthropic matches. Approximately half of our employees participate in this program. When combined with today’s announcement, roughly 20% of Anthropic shares will be dedicated to the public good, plus any additional percentage that could be added if the company reaches specific valuation milestones. In the coming months, we will share more about the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund’s structure and governance, including the valuation milestones that may add to its stake. We will also report on our progress to date against our mission in an upcoming public benefit report.

title: 突發！DeepSeek新模型釋出，超級價效比斬殺一切

Flash相比，1017版本在各項基準測試裡幾乎是整齊抬頭，程式碼、Agent任務等能力都有明顯提升。 但光漲分，還不算這次更新最狠的地方。 因為模型效能往上衝的同時， 任務執行時間和輸出長度反而被一起壓了下來 。 嗯？又要馬兒跑，又不給馬兒多吃草是吧？？ 官方把這個叫做“效能—費用的帕累託改進”，以前想讓Agent把活兒幹得更好，通常得接受它多想一會兒、多跑幾步、多吐點Token。 到了V4.1-Flash-1017這裡，模型開始嘗試少繞路、少說廢話，直接奔著把任務做完去。 從官方放出的DeepSWE測試來看，V4.1-Flash-1017已經在多個Agent框架下，把效能和成本之間的邊界繼續往外推了一截。 尤其是DeepSeek Harness、騰訊CodeBuddy和WorkBuddy，這回都吃到了專項最佳化。 目前要想把這套新能力完整吃上， DeepSeek Harness還得升級到0.2.1-rc.1及以上版本 。 “許願式程式設計一鍵成真” 當然，基準測試再漂亮，也不如直接看它能搓出什麼。 而DeepSeek這次給V4.1-Flash-1017準備的新活兒，名字也很懂網友—— “許願式程式設計” 。 怎麼個許願法？ 以前做一個完整專案，得先把功能、結構、互動和技術棧掰開了，一項項講給模型聽。 現在使用者只要說清楚自己想要什麼，剩下的規劃、寫程式碼、執行、檢查和修改，模型自己接著往下推。 背後的關鍵， 是一套基於自反饋的強化學習訓練技術 。 模型寫完第一版不會立刻下班，它會繼續檢查自己搓出來的東西，發現哪裡不對，再回頭修。 這套方法搓出來的結果如何呢？ 官方一上來就整了個大活，直接搓故宮。 D老師直接用程式碼搭出了一套可以即時瀏覽、切換視角的3D場景。 挺好，別人還在Vibe Coding做Todo List，D老師已經開始Vibe修故宮了。。。 而且後面一個比一個離譜： 網頁版賽車遊戲直接開跑，Godot版《傳送門2》復刻真能互動，還有一套橫跨史前到現代的動態3D世界。 從一句話，到一個能看、能動、能玩的完整專案。 “許願式程式設計”，這次還真讓D老師給許成了。 模型釋出前疑已洩露，“更聰明，也更簡潔了” 事實上，DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017早就漏得和篩子一樣了。 幾個小時前 ，就有眼尖的網友發現，DeepSeek的模型列表中，曾短暫出現“DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017”一項。 上架時間雖短，但還是被蹲更新的人逮了個正著。 “1017”正好對應 10月17日 ，也符合DeepSeek用日期標記模型快照的一貫方式。 緊接著，另一條證據也冒了出來。 有網友發現，deepseek-flash介面返回的系統指紋已經從“ aeb56401ca74e127821c4f9126dcb669”變成了“e72d3c7f663d3e1383b00b3884cb4501”。 系統指紋發生變化，通常意味著後臺服務的模型版本或部署配置已經更新。 而一輪體驗下來，目前比較一致的說法是： 新模型似乎更聰明、更快，輸出也更簡潔了 。 博主Chetaslua發現，右邊新版本生成出的畫面細節更加豐富，光影效果也更逼真。 一句話生成的效果也很不賴，還附有具體的創作過程。 原作者表示，比 Gemini 4 Argon 用起來更順暢。 從更多多模態結果來看，新模型似乎加強了 3D生成能力 。 博主Hakm公佈的幾組圖片，效果相當驚豔，已經有GPT-6 Astra釋出時給人的那種震撼了。 他還順手用模型生成了一款非常經典的槍戰遊戲。 秒哇！這波真有的看了。 自研搜尋API也開放了 不止如此，大肥魚這次也把Agent上網查資料的專用工具給咱們一併安排上了。 DeepSeek自研搜尋引擎正式推出 Search 和 Fetch 兩個API介面，前者負責搜網頁，後者用來讀正文。 開發者可以先讓Agent按照關鍵詞尋找資料，再把選中的網頁抓取成Markdown文本，交給模型繼續分析。 其中Search API還支援限定網站、語言和釋出時間，查最新訊息時，可以直接縮小範圍。 這部分的賬單費用也會按照成功請求次數單獨計價： 低到離譜，每千次成功請求均為 5元 ，單次使用僅需半分錢；如果請求失敗、搜尋無結果或超時，都通通不收費。 目前使用者已經可以在DeepSeek Harness、Claude Code或Codex中使用DeepSeek API時呼叫到，而且 限時到11月1日免費 。 title: 智譜新模型，懂法方面全球第一了
abstract: 智譜新模型，懂法方面全球第一了 文婷 2026-10-17 20:13:45 來源： 量子位 AI的風還是刮到了法律圈 文婷 發自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公眾號QbitAI 好傢伙，智譜把垂直模型，捲到法律圈了！ 就在剛剛，智譜推出了一款新的法律專用開源模型—— GLM-Legal 。 它不只能你聊聊法條，還能包攬審合同、串證據、做跨境合規研究等一系列具體的工作，並交給你一份可以原地使用的成果。 成績也相當能打。 在Vals AI最新公佈的法律測評中，GLM-Legal分別以 19.2% 的任務全通過率和 86.23% 的準確率，摘得Harvey LAB與LegalBench雙榜開放權重模型榜榜首。 好嘛，卷完聊天、辦公和程式碼還不夠，AI開始盯上法律合同和案卷裡的細活了。 訊息一齣，小夥伴們立馬坐不住了： 好好好，以後GLM-Legal就是我的法務團隊了。 但是Wait，它到底學的是哪國法律，真的能幫咱老中人幹活嗎？ 這就得展開看看了。 審合同、串證據、做合規，GLM-Legal都能接 好訊息是， 它確實適配咱們老中的法律 ，不會水土不服。 無論是中文法律實務、英文法律任務、還是東南亞跨境合規等考題，它都能接。 但模擬考終歸只是一方面。 真實法律工作中的坑可太多了，一踩一個不吱聲。 到底能不能幹活，咱們還是得把它拉進真實的法律工作環境裡溜溜，看看它能不能幫團隊審合同、確定海外發布前的隱私合規事項。 咱們先來看三組官方演示（ 論GLM-5.3-Flash大戰GLM-Legal，自己打自己 ）： 一、審合同，並把合作結束後的交接安排捋清楚 當咱們需要更換軟體服務供應商時，往往需要先審明白合同裡的終止和交接條款。 程式碼、資料、文件能不能順利拿回來？新供應商能不能接上？ 而這些雷，往往就埋在 條款 裡。 於是，GLM-Legal建議我們，把合作終止通知時間從60天縮短至30天，並增加最長90天的過渡支援，方便我們把程式碼、文件和知識交接都安排進去。 除此之外，它還結合合同已有的成果歸屬約定，要求交回全部的工作成果（包括尚未完成或尚未付款的部分）。 對比GLM-5.3-Flash，GLM-Legal的優勢就很明顯了： 前者只是給出較泛的建議，而GLM-Legal則進一步明確了時間、交接範圍等內容，並把修改方案與合同現有約定對應了起來。 好嘛，這套結束合作後的“分手流程”被它給寫明白了，非常之體面。 那我不禁想了，當我丟擲一堆散落的證據時，GLM-Legal又將如何應對呢？ 二、分析證據，並把散落的線索串起來 這其實是個很現實的問題。 當專案合作出現糾紛時，我們到底要怎樣才能從一堆海量的報告、文件和聊天記錄中判斷對方的說法有沒有問題？ 就比如官方給出的這個Case：對外報告稱專案完成了60%，內部記錄卻只有約41%。 在實測中，GLM-5.3-Flash和GLM-Legal都能發現這個矛盾點； 但不同的地方在於，GLM-5.3-Flash只給了建議，但GLM-Legal則在建議的基礎上，進一步將進度報告與更早的風險警告、內部溝通關聯了起來，並落地到了具體行動。 當這條線索梳理清楚了，咱們才方便回到原件逐項核對、並搞清楚到底哪個資料才是對的，可以繼續用下去的。 三、企業出海合規，把法規要求整理成行動清單 而當咱們準備在新加坡、馬來西亞和印度尼西亞等海外平臺上線網站時，可能會面對著使用者追蹤、郵件營銷、海外雲端儲存等每一項都可能涉及 隱私合規 的難題。 在這時候，我們可能就需要一個助手來幫我們搞清楚上線前究竟要做哪些準備。 對此，GLM-Legal在實測中把需要關注的合規事項，拆分成了團隊可以著手落實、繼續核查的細緻步驟，包括但不限於釋出具體隱私宣告、讓退訂請求輸入抑制列表等等，一目瞭然。 這下可方便多了。 所以沿著這個思路回頭看，咱們就能更直觀地明白Harvey LAB這個19.2%的全通過率到底難在哪、又值錢在哪了。 19.2%全通過，這張考卷有多難？ Harvey LAB的測評可從來不是紙老虎。 它採用了嚴苛的 “全條件通過”機制 ，只有當模型滿足了一項任務中的所有評分條件才算通過，少一條都不行。 它的任務設計也直接對標律所派活： 給Agent一個需求、一組客戶材料，並讓它直接整理出一份能拿來審閱的檔案。 其中光Harvey LAB首版，就設定了 超過1200項 模擬律所工作任務，覆蓋併購、智慧財產權、銀行金融等 24個 法律業務領域。 這意味著，模型從讀材料、調工具，到按規矩把結果交出來，這一路都不能掉鏈子，才能在這裡拿到一個不錯的分數。 而成績之外，還有一組測試賬單的反差值得咱們關注。 在成績相近的情況下，GLM-Legal比Gemini 4 Argon慢了近 30分鐘 、但Gemini的每項測試成本約為GLM-Legal的 70倍 ： 這一結果或許也提醒著咱們，在挑選法律工作搭子的時候，我們也得把成績、成本和時間得放在一起考慮。 那麼GLM-Legal究竟是怎樣訓練出來的？ 答案或許就藏在智譜一套配套的養成路徑裡。 不僅要讓AI讀法律，還要帶它進“律所”實習 智譜給GLM-Legal安排的成長路線，可以概括成一句話： 先送進“法學院”，再帶到“模擬律所”練手。 第一步 ，GLM-Lega會在GLM-5.3-Flash底座上進行法律語料中期訓練，並學習法律概念、法條和分析方法，打牢專業基礎。 第二步 ，GLM-Lega則需要通過數萬法律任務環境中的強化學習，不斷練習讀材料、做分析、推進任務和交付成果。 同時，團隊也在不斷迭代Agent執行框架，改進材料組織、工具連線和反饋流程，讓模型與工作環境一起磨合。 眼熟不？眼熟就對了！ 這不就是咱們法學生走過的打怪升級實錄嗎？！ 先考入大學法學院瘋狂啃書攢內功、然後在大三四大四一頭扎進律所當實習牛馬，最後熬過好幾年，甚至一路往上考，才終於能從小透明進化成靠譜的律師。 AI現在走的，正是咱們當年走過的路啊！ 只不過，GLM-Lega目前還處於相對青澀的實習牛馬階段罷了，咱還不能指望它上來就達到合夥人水平。 畢竟智譜這位“法律專才”現在還有許多需要繼續檢驗的地方，19.2%的全通過率也意味著它在嚴格評分條件下，多數任務仍未實現全部達標，目前還有很大的提升空間。 這也就對應了智譜現在的動作： 邀請律所、法律科技公司、企業法務團隊和獨立執業人士申請GLM-Legal Beta，並讓專業人士參與試用、提供反饋，共同打磨模型； 同時，智譜還計劃將相關能力接入AutoClaw，推進實際應用。 好傢伙，這背後傳遞出了一個清晰的訊號啊： 智譜正拉著一群最懂行的法律人打磨GLM-Lega，目標很明確，就是讓它在未來真正成為律師手裡得力的輔助工具。 而未來，智譜能不能真的實現這一願景，也值得咱們期待一波。 one more thing 其實智譜開卷法律模型，也並非心血來潮。 早在2023年，智譜就與專注智慧合同等業務的法律科技公司冪律智慧合作，基於ChatGLM-130B框架聯合研發並推出了一款千億參數級法律垂直模型 PowerLawGLM ，涉及法律諮詢、合同起草和審查等場景。 此後，智譜更是以老股東的身份，持續參與了冪律智慧的戰略融資和近8000萬元Pre-B輪融資。 而將通用模型送去“讀法律”的，也不止智譜。 早在今年8月，Harvey便聯手Fireworks，以Kimi K3為底座，後訓練出了一款自己的法律模型—— Tenet 。 據Harvey介紹，專項訓練後，它完成的LAB留出任務數量接近底座的兩倍，成本則保持穩定。 這些探索，或許也為行業提供了一些新思路，那就是： 選好通用底座後，再用專業任務、行業資料和工作環境繼續訓練，仍有機會把模型的能力繼續往前推一步。 而未來，誰能進一步把模型的“專業課”教得紮實，把“模擬律所”搭得更實用，讓它練出更多在真實工作中能用得上的本事，或許才能真正贏得這一圈層使用者的認可。 參考連結： [1] https://x.com/Zai_org/status/2109678174468534511?s=20 [2] https://z.ai/blog/glm-legal [3] title: 清華開源！智慧體作業系統任務成本降83%，AI記憶可查可改
abstract: 清華開源！智慧體作業系統任務成本降83%，AI記憶可查可改 夢瑤 2026-10-17 20:10:35 來源： 量子位 整套系統原生支援MCP 夢瑤 發自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公眾號 QbitAI 清華最近搞了個 開源智慧體作業系統 ，專治AI Agent幹活兒時的各種「老大難」問題？！ 這套名叫 PilotDeck 2.0 的系統，由清華大學THUNLP實驗室聯合面壁智慧、OpenBMB等團隊共同推出。 其解決的問題，好巧不巧的是正好和咱用AI Agent幹活兒時最扎心的事兒「強相關」—— 就比如啊…專案一多，檔案、記憶、任務全攪在一起，傻眼捏…（笑） 活一複雜，Token嘩嘩往外燒，人剛離開電腦，AI又卡在半路等指令*1000…… 而PilotDeck 2.0瞄準的，恰好就是這些讓人頭大的老bug—— 記憶管理、任務執行，以及模型呼叫成本 。 貼心的我，也幫大家淺淺總結了一下這玩意兒到底能幫咱們幹啥事兒，能解決啥日常的麻煩—— 專案管理 ：同時處理多個專案，隔離檔案、記憶與任務，減少資料混雜、任務串臺。 長期記憶 ：記住專案背景、使用者偏好和工作進度，支援檢視與修改，避免反覆交代。 後臺執行 ：支援後臺執行長週期任務、檢查可執行事項，讓AI在使用者離開時繼續幹活。 智慧路由 ：據任務難度選擇合適的模型，複雜任務用強模型、簡單任務用低成本模型，減少不必要的開支。 在Workbuddy Bench評測表現上，PilotDeck使用Qwen3.6-35B-A3B得分79.1，也優於Claude Code (77.3)。 此外，通過讓強模型管決策、小模型幹雜活的排程方式，還能把複雜長任務的成本砍掉近六分之五？？ 聽上去，好像，還蠻實用的，哈？？？ AI有了自己的工作艙，記憶、檔案和任務都能管起來了 大家或許都有這種感覺… 就咱平時用各種AI工具，最害怕的事情之一就是「上下文汙染」。 比如前腳剛讓AI按嚴肅學術風寫了篇技術架構，後腳讓它寫小紅書文案，它張口閉口還是架構解耦。。。（笑） 而這抓馬之事的背後，主要是和現有的大多數Agent記憶的黑盒問題有關係。 換句話說，AI到底記住了什麼、什麼時候記的、記在哪了，螢幕這頭的我們兩眼一抹黑。 萬一中途記錯了某個關鍵業務邏輯，想找到問題出在哪兒都費勁，最後只能忍痛把整段對話廢掉，從頭再來！！！ 而PilotDeck最核心的底層架構，就是以WorkSpace（工作艙）為基本單位。 我們可以把它理解成給AI劃分了獨立的物理工位，每個專案都有自己專屬的檔案系統、記憶庫和技能集。 具體官方給出的例子—— 在A工作艙裡折騰音影片剪輯，在B工作艙裡iOS小遊戲，兩邊的記憶和檢索空間完全物理隔離，再也不會互相打架。 這樣一來，即便同時處理好幾攤活兒，也能各自保留上下文，減少記憶串臺、任務跑偏的麻煩： 更擊中痛點的是，PilotDeck把記憶徹底做成了「白盒化」。 比如AI突然說我記得你之前偏好這種寫法，你可能根本不知道它從哪兒得出的結論，也不知道它有沒有記錯！！ 白盒記憶解決的就是這個問題，直接給了使用者一個隨時「翻賬本」的機會—— 從記憶的生成、抽取、儲存到最後被呼叫，整條鏈路完全對使用者可見。 比如AI在幹活兒過程中記下了哪些偏好、哪些事實，點開面板就能一條條檢視。 萬一發現它把某個關鍵參數記錯了，也不用費勁巴拉地寫一長串Prompt，試圖讓它忘掉錯誤資訊。 直接手動修改、刪除，甚至可以一鍵固定重要資訊就行～ 此外，其還內建了一個叫「Dream模式」的機制。 當AI處於空閒狀態時，系統會在後臺自動對零散的互動記憶進行歸納、提煉和去重。 如果整理過程中弄丟了關鍵細節，還能一鍵回滾，秒級恢復到整理前的狀態，不用擔心越整理越亂。 不僅如此，PilotDeck還引入了Always-on（常駐執行） 模式—— 即使關掉聊天視窗、離開電腦，Agent依然會在後臺持續推進長週期的監控與執行任務。 能把既定任務跑完，還能在執行過程中主動發現潛在的候選任務，並在全部搞定之後，把成果落地為本地檔案，附帶一份完整的進展與總結報告。 值得一提的是，整套系統原生支援MCP。 不管習慣在Web介面、命令列CLI還是企業微信、飛書等IM生態裡操作，後端的邏輯和行為完全一致。 對開發者來說，意味著可以圍繞現有工作流擴展工具和技能。 對長期使用AI的友友來說，也算是有機會減少反覆交代背景、手動串聯步驟的時間～ 「主強子弱」智慧路由：花1/6的錢，把頂配模型幹趴下。。。 用Agent跑長任務，錢包扛不住往往是最大的勸退點。 很多時候任務並不難，可能只是把幾段文字做個排版、把多語種翻譯套個模板—— 但是吧，因為系統架構簡陋，全程都在狂跑最貴的旗艦模型，Token消耗往往還蠻誇張的。。。 值得一提的是，PilotDeck還搞了個Smart Routing（智慧路由）。 其在底層內建了任務難度識別，把不同環節的任務拆解後分發給不同段位的模型，做了一套端雲協同與分層編排。 複雜的規劃決策讓頂配大模型來做，底層的執行、潤色、格式處理全部降級給輕量模型。 在自媒體社媒運營場景的實測中，如果不做省錢路由，全流程跑Claude Opus 4.5，單次費用高達$12.58。 而開啟智慧路由後，主Agent負責頂層規劃走Opus 4.5，子Agent負責文本潤色降級到Sonnet 4.5。 費用降到$2.83，差不多能省下70%的成本，be like： 此外，在更硬核的複雜任務測試中，這個差距體現的更懸殊一些？？ 研究團隊拿播客多語言推送、多源資料包告、領域論文綜述、程式碼庫架構文件等7個高難度複雜任務做了橫向對比： 單體MiniMax-M2.7跑下來，成本是挺低（$1.90），但得分只有37.1，沒法用，直接pass。。。 單體Claude Sonnet 4.6跑下來，得分衝到了69.1，但一趟測試就要燒掉$18.36。 而在PilotDeck的路由編排下，採用主Sonnet 4.6+子MiniMax-M2.7的主強子弱架構，綜合得分飆到了70.6，成本只要$3.15。 效果比純頂配單體模型好的同時，成本卻只有頂配模型的六分之一左右。 對了，PilotDeck採用AGPL-3.0開源許可證，支援macOS、Linux和Windows，也提供Docker部署方式。 大家感興趣的話，可以上手試試，GitHub連結放下面了哈～ 參考連結： [1] https://github.com/OpenBMB/PilotDeck [2] title: Claude半小時解開密碼學懸案，學界集體走偏20年
abstract: Claude半小時解開密碼學懸案，學界集體走偏20年 鷺羽 2026-10-17 20:06:51 來源： 量子位 謎底指向時間 鷺羽 發自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公眾號QbitAI 一大早的，AI圈又炸了。。。 無他，AI這波解題潮，已經往前翻到了密碼學界二十多年的舊賬。 全員大逃殺，這次輪到 Claude —— 剛剛，據Anthropic披露，Claude用 不到半小時 ，查明瞭五條NIST標準橢圓曲線的種子生成方式。 這串業界用了二十多年的數字，一度被寫進密碼學標準，但最初是怎麼選出來的，一直沒人能說清。 人們甚至找到了當事人，線索指向一句 “給Bob和Jerry加薪” 的口令雜湊運算。 結果戲劇性的來了，Claude說：大錯特錯！ 真正的答案，來自 時間 ，一款90年代的電腦時鐘。 而且這樁懸案，已經得到了懸賞發起人的獨立複核。 半小時破解密碼學懸案 事情還得從一套用來“驗明正身”的技術說起。 ECDSA ，全稱橢圓曲線數字簽名演算法。 它能讓接收方檢查，一份資料是否由聲稱的簽署者簽發，以及簽署後有沒有被修改。2000年，它被美國國家標準與技術研究院NIST納入FIPS 186-2數字簽名標準。 使用這套演算法之前，還得先選定一些公共數學參數，包括曲線P-192、P-224、P-256、P-384和P-521。 爭議就出自它們的 種子 上。 可以把種子理解為生成曲線參數的起始材料：拿到種子，按照標準規定的步驟運算，就能檢查後面的參數是否對得上。 但 為什麼偏偏是這個種子 ，壓根沒人知道。 就連當年提供種子的Jerry Solinas也已經記憶模糊，只大致記得，他們曾把一句可能是加薪的玩笑口令轉換成數字，再加了計數器。 於是這二十多年來，大家都在往這個方向猜，密碼學工程師Filippo Valsorda還發布了 懸賞令 ，高調邀請大家尋找這五組種子的前身。 結果都是無疾而終，直到 Claude 出手了。 按照Anthropic的描述，員工在把問題交給內部研究模型時，並沒有告知這條加薪口令的線索。 Claude於是自行猜測，這些數字也許來自 90年代C語言庫 裡的偽隨機數生成器。 因為這類程式生成的數字看似雜亂，背後卻遵循固定規律。只要認出規律，就有機會倒推出生成過程。 隨後Claude寫了一個 掃描程式 ，把公開種子裡的二進位制數字一位位挪著檢查，測試了34種生成器與輸出擷取方式的組合。 結果發現，四組種子分別拆成五個32位整數後，這20個整數的最高位， 居然全是0 。 破案了，嫌疑人應該是 lrand48隨機數生成器 。 lrand48內部儲存著一個48位整數，每呼叫一次，它就把這個整數乘上固定常數，再加上另一個常數，最後只保留結果的低48位，作為下一輪狀態。 但輸出結果只有其中的高31位，如果放進32位裡，剩下的則只能用0來補。 找到了機器後，Claude再借助 LLL格基約簡演算法 恢復種子被擷取狀態。 接下來就只剩一個問題，最初是如何啟動的？ 負責初始化的函式叫srand48，它會把輸入值放進48位狀態的高32位，再把低16位固定設為0x330E，再沿著遞推關係往回算，目標指向 Unix時間戳 。 這些初始化輸入，集中落在了 1997年5月至1998年4月 。 也就是說， 把某一刻的時間變成整數 ，交給生成器，再按固定方式取出數字，就能重新得到標準裡的種子。 以P-256為例，對應的初始化時刻是：1997年8月16日，UTC時間01:52:34。 從這個時間出發運行生成器，取第1842組候選，得到的正是那串以C49D開頭的種子。另外四組也能一一對應上。 當然，A社也表示，這份結果還沒有補齊所有歷史空白。 研究者發現，當年的程式跳過了一些看起來也符合條件的候選曲線，原因仍不明確；B-163的種子，以及部分曲線基點的生成方式，也尚未得到解釋。 不過新結果也意味著這些曲線並不存在任何潛在的安全漏洞，可以放心食用。 參考連結： [1] https://www.anthropic.com/research/ecdsa-curve-origins [2] https://x.com/sweis/status/2111165738836717980 [3] https://words.filippo.io/seeds-bounty/ 版權所有，未經授權不得以任何形式轉載及使用，違者必究。 Claude 密碼學 鷺羽 突發！DeepSeek新模型釋出，超級價效比斬殺一切 2026-10-17 這個雙十一，百靈新模型幹起活來不燒心 2026-10-15 矽谷AI現狀：誰有算力誰是爹 2026-10-11 何愷明團隊新作：看貓片就能學會ARC挑戰 2026-10-01 相關閱讀

title: 科技企業出海，為啥我推薦你去迪拜？
abstract: 科技企業出海，為啥我推薦你去迪拜？ 一水 2026-10-17 17:05:08 來源： 量子位 通往全球市場的超級跳板 林方舟 發自 凹非寺 量子位 | 公眾號QbitAI 全體都有！準備出海的科技公司們，向這裡看齊！ 剛剛， 迪拜商業論壇·中國 在深圳落下帷幕，AI主題論壇上，那叫一個座無虛席～ 情況不難理解：AI現在是全世界的香餑餑，企業一方面得跟上國內市場卷的速度，另一方面全球市場的大蛋糕也得佈局呀。 過去，中國的手機、家電席捲海外市場；如今，中國的智慧汽車，漸漸成為老外的Dream Car；而未來，中國的AI基建和產品，也將在全球市場拿到大結果。 如今，迪拜張開雙臂，熱烈歡迎中國AI等科技企業前來，有出海想法的企業們，真的可以認真考慮一下。 Why？ 迪拜是全球最國際化的城市之一，外籍人士占人口的85%以上，“開放包容”一直是金字招牌。 迪拜現代、宜居、富有活力，不僅對科技等新興產業捨得砸錢，營商環境也比較靠譜。 更關鍵的是，迪拜地處歐亞非三大洲交匯點，這裡不只是企業出海的一站，還是拓展中東、非洲及歐洲市場的支點。 迪拜豪華代表團來華 繼2024年北京站後，這是迪拜商業論壇第二次來到中國，迪拜代表團的陣仗可謂相當之大。 共有100餘位迪拜政企核心代表前來，是迪拜商會迄今參加國際活動以來規模最大的代表團。 代表團由迪拜商會會長領銜，成員包括迪拜經濟發展局、迪拜環球港務集團、阿聯酋航空等頂級機構的高階代表。 迪拜參會人員多為公司創始人、董事長與CEO。他們手握資本、物流與渠道資源，是能拍板的一號位。 他們此次前來，可不是走馬觀花式的考察，而是帶著合作誠意來的。 論壇期間，各方共簽署10項合作備忘錄，覆蓋貿易投資促進、科技創新及產業協作等領域。 論壇議程方面，AI和科技是絕對C位。 從智慧體AI、雲端計算和數字基礎設施，到自動駕駛與未來出行，多場討論談的都是AI和科技帶來的機遇。 中國多數頭部大型科技服務商已經在迪拜佈局。本次論壇上，不少中國AI和先進製造業公司，分享了在迪拜跑通商業閉環的經驗。 比如百度的Apollo Go，已經在迪拜開啟全無人駕駛商業運營，拿到了迪拜首張全無人駕駛測試許可。 來看兩個資料：2025年，迪拜進口的電動乘用車中超過85%都來自中國；而迪拜2030年交通戰略提出，25%的出行由自動駕駛完成。 國內卷瘋了的車企們，機會這不就來了嗎～ 雲廠商們也在發力。騰訊雲和阿聯酋科技企業合作，推動超級APP生態建設，探索整合數字錢包和跨境支付功能；華為雲和中東支付公司合作，共同開發數字支付相關技術。 迪拜此前設立目標： 十年內外貿規模達到7萬億美元，吸引外商直接投資1770億美元。 這麼大的蛋糕，就問你香不香？ 迪拜押注AI和數字經濟 為何迪拜這麼重視AI和數字經濟？ 如果你對迪拜的印象還停留在“石油土豪”，那可就大錯特錯了。 迪拜一直在擺脫對傳統產業的依賴。 它正在從全球貿易樞紐，轉型為全球數字經濟中心。 阿聯酋此前設定了一個極具野心的目標： 十年內將數字經濟對GDP的貢獻率，從2022年的9.7%直接翻倍至19.4%。 迪拜則推出了“D33經濟議程”。其中目標之一是 通過數字化轉型，每年創造1000億迪拉姆（約合1800億元人民幣）的經濟價值。 要實現這樣的目標，AI就得進入企業的業務流程。客服、採購、銷售、物流，都要找到能改善效率的具體環節。 於是，輪到AI Agent上場了。 今年5月，迪拜宣佈啟動一項重磅舉措： 兩年智慧體AI（Agentic AI）倡議 。 根據該計劃，迪拜商會將推動智慧體AI技術在迪拜商界的廣泛應用，賦能超過29.5萬家私營企業，並在兩年內開發和推出100個專業AI助手，幫助企業提升相關技術的實際應用能力。 目前，迪拜商會正面向1.4萬家私營企業開展智慧體AI應用培訓。 title: 🗞️China Proposes AI Export Controls, DeepSeek Bets on Robotics, and Infinigence Raises $334M
abstract: China AI Weekly Digest summarizes the week’s big news, model updates, policy, products, and research, sourced from the aggregated newsfeed of China AI Index. The digest below is mostly compiled and drafted by an AI agent sourcing from credible news outlets, then fact-checked and edited by me. This week: 313 stories tracked (0 editor picks, 86 English-language, 227 Chinese-language 🇨🇳) over 2026-10-10–2026-10-17. China proposes export controls on advanced AI technologies, with important exceptions for overseas services. China’s commerce and science ministries proposed adding AI models, agents, chip designs and computing clusters to its technology export-control catalogue. This is a draft, not an enacted blanket ban on Chinese AI going abroad. The commerce ministry’s accompanying explanation draws a distinction: transferring restricted technology overseas would fall within the framework, while providing access through APIs, apps, web interfaces or SaaS would not constitute a large-model technology export. It also proposes facilitation for open-source activity and excludes technology already in the public domain. The final definitions will matter for labs releasing weights, building overseas infrastructure and serving international customers. ( Bloomberg / FT / 商務部 ) DeepSeek reportedly moves into robotics investing through Winverse AI. DeepSeek is reportedly preparing to lead a seed financing for Winverse AI, the robotics-AI startup founded by former Tencent scientist Hu Han. Meituan’s Long-Z Investments is also among the reported participants. Terms remain subject to change. For DeepSeek, this would extend its involvement beyond supplying general-purpose models into backing a team developing intelligence for robots. Other Chinese tech giants like ByteDance, Alibaba, Ant, alongside LLM startups, have also poured investments into robotics. ( Bloomberg / 虎嗅 ) Infinigence closes a $334M round to expand its AI infrastructure business. Infinigence AI completed a RMB2.3 billion Series C, bringing cumulative financing to RMB4.3 billion. Its business spans three connected layers: pooling and scheduling heterogeneous compute, serving models through a “Token factory,” and delivering industry-specific agent solutions. The company’s model platform offers more than 100 models and works with developers including Z.ai and Moonshot. Those details explain what investors are financing: infrastructure that connects hardware capacity to usable inference and enterprise workloads. ( 量子位 / 愛範兒 ) This week brought new weight releases, a broader video-model rollout and more specialized offerings. DeepSeek released V4.1-Flash-1017, updating its website, app and API and publishing MIT-licensed weights. The multimodal model retains a 1M-token context window; DeepSeek reports improved coding and agent performance with shorter outputs and faster task completion, including 77.0 on DeepSWE v1.1 using Mini-SWE-V2. ( DeepSeek / Hugging Face ) StepFun released Step 5 Preview’s BF16 and FP8 weights on Hugging Face and ModelScope. The company describes a 600-billion-parameter MoE with 27 billion active parameters, native text-and-vision input and a one-million-token context window. This is an open-weight release of the existing preview. ( @StepFun_ai ) Ant opened Ling-3.1-flash, following its earlier announcement. The model features approximately 560 billion total parameters and 25 billion active per token. ( 36Kr / @AntLingAGI ) Kling 4.0 moved to its formal rollout, with coverage highlighting native 30-second generation and 10-bit HDR. This follows September early access, rather than marking its first announcement. Availability of individual resolution and output features should be distinguished from the overall release. ( 36Kr ) Z.ai introduced GLM-Legal, built on GLM-5.3-Flash, for contract review, evidence analysis and compliance workflows. Its announcement invites applications for API access; it does not establish unrestricted availability. ( @Zai_org ) Kimi K3 topped the first ranking from RSI, the self-improvement benchmark startup backed by Jeff Dean. ( 36Kr ) Infrastructure spending continued to attract financing, while some large rounds remained unsettled. Tencent told investors its planned $5 billion bond financing would primarily support AI capital expenditure. Subsequent Chinese reporting put the priced dollar-and-renminbi notes at approximately RMB38 billion in total. The initial dollar-equivalent target and the final multi-currency issuance should be kept distinct. ( Bloomberg / 財聯社 ) DeepSeek’s own fundraising continued to generate headlines about a possible RMB100 billion round. Reporting that prospective investors were still seeking entry points indicates the process remained fluid; the target should not be presented as a completed raise. ( 財聯社 ) Moonshot executives are in talks to settle the shareholder dispute with Recurrent ahead of the planned Hong Kong listing, per Reuters. ( MarketScreener ) Citi says China AI supply-chain IPOs are holding firm despite the valuation pullback. ( Reuters ) Agent permissions and safety governance became concrete operating issues. ByteDance established a dedicated AI safety team and launched an international hiring drive. Chinese coverage describes safety and alignment becoming a separate department within Seed, giving the organizational announcement more substance than a general commitment to responsible AI. ( Reuters / 雷峰網 ) More than 150 apps reportedly declined GUI-based automated operation through Doubao Phone Assistant’s proposed access framework. The dispute concerns whether agents can act inside other companies’ apps—a permissions and commercial-access problem that better model performance alone cannot resolve. ( 虎嗅 ) Taiwan plans tighter AI-chip export restrictions to China as part of its US trade arrangements, Bloomberg reported. This is a separate development from Beijing’s proposed controls on outbound Chinese technology. ( Bloomberg ) Office agents gained workflow integrations, while AI moved further into phones and wearable hardware. STEPX Neo’s early edition launched at RMB3,999, combining the handset with Step AOS, Step Studio and access to Step models. The positioning targets developers and early adopters building agent-native applications; it should not be mistaken for evidence that every advertised cross-app workflow is already broadly supported. ( 量子位 ) Tencent connected WorkBuddy with WeCom, allowing it to appear as a conversational colleague and use authorized workplace context. Separately, WorkBuddy Enterprise added an observability center for organizations managing agent use. These are workflow and administration updates, rather than new foundation models. ( 雷峰網 / 雷峰網 ) Qwen Work introduced an e-commerce edition through invitation testing, aimed at merchants managing operations across stores and platforms. Alibaba also opened applications for Qwen Go, a separate agent offering; that remains an announced experience awaiting broader availability. ( 雷峰網 / 雷峰網 ) Doubao Work added a way to import existing configurations from other AI products. It is a practical attempt to reduce migration friction for users who have already invested time setting up another assistant. ( 雷峰網 ) Alibaba unveiled AI glasses priced at approximately $450, extending its hardware push. The announcement adds a wearable interface to its AI distribution strategy. ( Bloomberg ) Baidu’s Hong Kong robotaxi trial is set to include more than 1,000 members of the public. Separately, Pony.ai announced Manchester testing with Uber and Verne, following its London plans. ( SCMP / @PonyAI_tech ) The week’s other earthquake was in memory. CXMT described progress on a 4F² DRAM cell architecture using vertical surrounding-gate transistors. The announcement concerns a denser memory-cell design; it does not, by itself, demonstrate production yield, qualified customer shipments or a performance lead over Korean competitors.

title: Anthropic gives outside AI watchdog “employee-like” access
abstract: Anthropic has granted external evaluators “employee-like access” to assess the risks of its models, following through on a commitment to increase safeguards over concerns the technology could run catastrophically out of control. METR, a nonprofit that has worked with leading labs including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Meta, now has a team embedded in the Claude maker’s office with access to its hardware and internal systems. A greater role for third-party evaluators is among the main concrete steps the labs have proposed in response to rising concern about the dangers more capable AI systems could pose to the economy, cyber security and humanity at large. Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei achieved a rare moment of unity with arch-rivals Sam Altman and Elon Musk in September when the OpenAI and SpaceX bosses rallied behind his proposal to embed external auditors in the leading labs. Thursday’s announcement marks the first step to implementing these pledges. OpenAI has yet to lay out plans to bring in evaluators after Altman said Amodei’s proposals were a good idea. “As models have become more powerful, they’ve required stronger safeguards and more challenging risk assessment,” Anthropic said on Thursday. “We want to be publicly accountable for the decisions we’re making. But we can’t publicly share all the information relevant to our safety work.” Critics of Anthropic’s proposal to use evaluators have argued the arrangements could lead to conflicts of interest, pointing to issues in the accounting sector, and that greater government regulation is required. Anthropic argued that sharing information publicly could benefit malicious actors or competitors and added that its evaluators will operate similarly to bank supervision, whereby regulators assign resident examiners to work inside the largest banks.

The phrase "told investors" appears four times in this FT article, which reports on Anthropic's day of hosting investors on Wednesday. Lots of details in here from " people with knowledge of the matter ". Key things I learned from the article: This point about distillation is worth quoting in full (highlight mine): The start-up has also clamped down on “distillation” — a controversial practice whereby rival AI labs train their models on the outputs of more advanced ones. When rival companies “distil” their models from Anthropic’s models, that involves heavy usage and spending. Anthropic told investors on Wednesday distillation accounted for 5 per cent to 7 per cent of revenue and that they had cut it back “materially” in the third quarter of the year, said four people with direct knowledge of the matter. Napkin maths says that if distillation was 5% of their Q2 revenue (before they cut it back in Q3) then unnamed "other labs" spent over half a billion dollars distilling Anthropic's models in that quarter! Also notable: Anthropic appear to no longer be leaning on "annualized run-rate revenue" ( previously ) in these communications to their investors. # 15th October 2026 , 1:04 pm / ai , generative-ai , llms , anthropic AI is mass decompiling games. That’s both awesome and scary. ( via ) Indie game developer Popcar talks about the recent wave of AI-powered decompilation of existing games, enabling weird mashups between existing games, and producing a boom in game preservation projects to get old games working on new hardware (often in a browser using WebAssembly). I like how this piece captures both the positives and the negatives of this new development: Most people already realized the scary part by now. If AI can decompile games and software, then the entire tech industry is about to explode. Anybody can decompile other software and use it any way they'd like, and nobody can stop them. Companies can steal from competitors. Your paid game or app can be open-sourced against your will. This isn't exclusive to old video games, we can apply this to any software. [...] This is also a big win for preservation. Old games can be ported, modified, enhanced, and made much more easily accessible than before. [...[ With console makers going all in on digital and games becoming entirely unplayable due to servers shutting down, this is fantastic news. We could own software we bought regardless of what the company thinks. # 14th October 2026 , 4:26 pm / computer-history , game-design , ai , webassembly , generative-ai , llms , ai-ethics , coding-agents Redesigning source control at Anthropic ( via ) Interesting piece from Anthropic describing why and how they built their own custom alternative to Git, based on the dramatic increase in rate of changes to their code after the past six months. In May 2026, Anthropic averaged around 2,500 code changes merged per day; as of September, we merged over 30,000 per day. They included a chart showing those changes. I had Claude modify their chart ( code here ) to add markers for the public releases of each of their models in 2026: This shows public release dates, not the date when models became available for Anthropic's internal use. My guess is that the introduction of Fable/Mythos class models is a key factor in the increased coding velocity. "Antique" is their new code review system. The source control system is called Scion, and sounds to me like a reinvention of centralized source control along the lines of Subversion. ( Update : Anthropic credit Google's Piper and Meta's Sapling as "prior art" - it looks like the core concept of "derived data" was heavily inspired by Mononoke , the server component of Sapling.) They had some pretty extreme requirements: The history of our main branch alone is almost 100 GB, and a compressed working copy is over 25 GB. We perform on the order of 25 million code checkouts per day for CI, before counting developer environments, agent sandboxes, and research jobs. Fetched naively, that would be over 600 PB of git traffic per day. The new system was built by a team of seven people, and the migration from Git was completed in five months. When asked on Hacker News about the lack of offline support, Scion engineer Nick G replied : Since Claude is by far the heaviest user of Scion and is necessarily online, this just wasn't important to do. As an aside, I've been trying adversarial review in my own projects recently, where you have a model try and find flaws (I often play Claude and GPT off against each other). Bit of a niche link, but I've been waiting for this for a couple of days - I even told ChatGPT to check for it: Clone https://github.com/actions/python-versions and git pull once an hour until they add the stable 3.15 - then tell me about it Now that this has landed, you can add "3.15" to a GitHub Actions testing matrix to run tests against the new Python 3.15.0 release . # 10th October 2026 , 11:58 pm / github , python , github-actions , chatgpt Deno is joining Cloudflare ( via ) The Deno team released the first version of celld back in August - their open source implementation of the Durable Objects pattern from Cloudflare Workers. Today, Cloudflare are acquiring Deno outright, with the goal of building on celld to "make workerd self-hosting a first-class supported way to build and run apps using the Workers programming model" (see the Cloudflare blog .) The bad news is that Deno itself will not be maintained by Cloudflare beyond the next year: We will support the Deno runtime for another year with monthly releases containing bug fixes and security updates. After that year we will end our development of the Deno runtime. Deno will remain open source, and we welcome others who want to continue its development. Deno (and Node.js) creator Ryan Dahl explained that decision in a comment on Hacker News: It's a joint decision and I agree with it. I'm most invested in its success and have put the most work into it - and I no longer think it's where I can do the most important work. There are some good ideas in Deno and it's well engineered - but it ultimately is not solving big problems. It has been sucked into the gravity well of node compatibility, which forces it to behave exactly as Node does. Why reimplement Node? It works. Marginal performance or UX or security benefits are not enough. I'm interested in building powerful new abstractions. celld has been working remarkably well, depending only on object storage for coordination and persistence. It is not just a slightly different API to interact with the file system or network - it's an entirely new model for server development. My favorite feature of Deno has long been the permissions system, where you can run a Deno script and specify exactly which files and folders it can read and write to, and which network hosts it can access. The OpenAI Codex desktop app (since rebranded to just ChatGPT) has 1.7GB of stuff in there in a folder called codex-primary-runtime , including a full Python installation, a full Node.js installation, and native binaries for Poppler , git, and the LibreOffice open source office suite (which forked from OpenOffice.org in 2010): The ~/.cache/codex-runtimes/codex-primary-runtime/plugins/openai-primary-runtime/plugins/documents folder includes skills which tell Codex how to find and use those binaries. # 1st September 2026 , 7:03 pm / codex , generative-ai , openai , ai , llms , openoffice , open-source The key skill required to make productive use of coding agents is being able to confidently instruct them on how to make changes and then confidently verify that those changes have been applied in the correct way. Eyeballing every line of code has never been the most effective way to validate a change to a piece of software. # 22nd August 2026 , 3:56 pm / code-review , coding-agents , generative-ai , agentic-engineering , ai , llms I started building my markdown-svg-renderer tool in May , but I've since added enough features to it that it's worth talking about here again. It's evolved into my ideal tool for sharing Markdown transcripts that include SVG documents. Given my proclivity for drawing pelicans riding bicycles this is a problem that I needed to solve! The tool is very simple. Navigate to markdown-svg-renderer in your browser and paste in some Markdown to see it rendered... or save that Markdown to a CORS-friendly URL or a GitHub Gist and paste in a URL to that document. The URL option will give you a bookmarkable page, for example https://tools.simonwillison.net/markdown-svg-renderer#url=https%3A%2F%2Fgist.github.com%2Fsimonw%2F6f9e48293be5c916652d29f0dc0b0657 - which bakes in the URL to this Gist . If you visit the Gist you'll see raw SVG: In the rendered tool that looks like this instead: As you can see, that SVG block in the Markdown has been transformed into a rendered SVG (in this case animated) plus several tabs. The tabs are the really fun bit. The PNG and JPEG tabs render that SVG to those image formats in the browser and lets you copy or download them - useful for sharing on platforms that don't support SVG directly. The MP4 tab is new today - it examines the SVG to see if it contains any animations, attempts to guess how long the looped video should be, then renders a whole bunch of frames of the animation and loads 30+MB of ffmpeg.wasm so it can compile those frames into an MP4 video using the full power of FFMPEG compiled to WebAssembly and running in the browser. Being able to turn an animated SVG into a MP4 again makes it easy to share on platforms that can't support SVG animation natively. It's a neat trick! # 16th August 2026 , 11:59 pm / svg , markdown , tools I wrote this summary of the past few weeks of open letters as a section of my sponsors-only newsletter but I've decided to share it here as well. Open Weights and American AI Leadership was shepherded by Microsoft, dated July 24th, and signed by 235 AI-adjacent companies including NVIDIA (see Jensen's first ever tweet ), Amazon, Y Combinator, The Linux Foundation, and (a later signer) OpenAI. It's clearly an argument designed to counter any instincts by the current US government to ban or limit open weight models over "safety" concerns - a reasonable consideration given what happened to Claude Fable 5 ! Relying solely on closed models is not inherently safe: they can be breached, misused, or fail in ways that outsiders cannot detect. And concentrating advanced AI capabilities behind a small number of closed models compounds that risk. It results in a small number of single points of failure, weakens competition, and leaves critical technology in the hands of a few providers. Open weight models, on the other hand, allow a broad community of researchers and developers to examine their behavior, identify vulnerabilities, develop safeguards, and improve them over time. The one surprising note in the letter is that it comes out in support of distillation, where models train on output from other models: In shaping this ecosystem, policymakers should be careful not to conflate legitimate model-development techniques with misappropriation. Distillation, or the practice of using one model’s outputs to help train or improve another, is a widely used technique for model improvement, evaluation, and validation.

Tiny Little Office's signature trick is to store all of the document data in the #fragment section of the URL, so every document created using it becomes a bookmarkable and shareable link. Here's the sequence of prompts I used: I want a tool where you can link to it with a fragment hash #code-here and it treats that code as LaTeX and renders it really effectively. It should also support a prefix which means the latex is compressed with a custom compression dictionary optimized for latex. Use the best available latex render library from a CDN (consider WebAssembly too). If loaded without a fragment hash show an editor you can paste latex into and then toggle to a "rendered" view. That rendered view should be bookmarkable. The #fragment view should let you switch to edit source too. Since it was working in my tools repo I told it to take inspiration from the mechanism used by my existing SVG in Markdown tool as protection against XSS risks: Safe from XSS? The tool uses Pako 2.1.0 , MathJax 4.1.3 , faster-latex 0.3.1 , and DOMPurify 3.4.16 . Another game experiment with Claude. This one used the default Claude iPhone app (chat mode, not Claude Code mode), where I prompted Claude Opus 5.5 Max with: Build a three js game called "Tree appreciator" - it shows you two algorithmically generated trees and the game mechanics is about appreciating the differences between them. Think hard about how to make sure it is both fun and beautiful. Somewhat embarrassingly given my recent talk , I've found that telling Opus 5.5 "make sure it is fun" works uncomfortably well. In this case Claude crunched for 3 hours and 7 minutes before retuning a cosy little spot-the-difference game with music and animation and achievements that's quite compelling to play. I added support to llm-gemini for the new Gemini 4 Argon model, made available today via the Gemini API and for customers of their $100/month subscription plan. Here's the "high" illustration, which cost me 17.166 cents: The pricing is interesting. At launch, Argon is $2/million input and $10/million output - the same price as GPT-6 Sol, half the price of Claude Opus 5.5 and 1/5th the price of Claude Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra. But on December 1st Argon is set to double in price - so it will be the same price as Opus 5.5. Prices like this aren't really comparable these days since what really matters is how many tokens a model takes to achieve a goal within an agentic harness. One useful clue for that comes from Artificial Analysis, who publish the total cost to run their benchmark using each model. Argon is looking very good there - costing $2,407 to run the benchmark, putting it close to GLM-5.3 and significantly cheaper than OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta's latest models. These look like they may be Meta's first Fable class models - Artificial Analysis scores Muse Wonder (Max) as equivalent to GPT-6.1 Sol. I updated my llm-meta-ai plugin for the new model. Here are pelicans for Muse Wonder for the six reasoning levels: minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max. This is the max one: For comparison, here are pelicans for Muse 1.3 (released September 2nd) and Muse 1.2 (released August 5th). title: Comfy-Org/ComfyUI
abstract: ComfyUI The most powerful and modular AI engine for content creation. ComfyUI is the AI creation engine for visual professionals who demand control over every model, every parameter, and every output. Its powerful and modular node graph interface empowers creatives to generate images, videos, 3D models, audio, and more... ComfyUI natively supports the latest open-source state of the art models. It is by far the most optimized inference engine for diffusion models in the world with a focus on local consumer hardware. Can run even the biggest open source models on as low as 4GB vram + 8GB ram relatively quickly (saturating your GPU compute) using our state of the art asynchronous weight streaming technology. Partner nodes provide access to the best closed source models such as Nano Banana, Seedance, Hunyuan3D, etc. It is available on Windows, Linux, and macOS, locally with our desktop application , our portable install or on our cloud . The most sophisticated workflows can be exposed through a simple UI thanks to App Mode. It integrates seamlessly into production pipelines with our API endpoints. Get Started Local Desktop Application The easiest way to get started. Available on Windows & macOS. Manual Install Supports all operating systems and GPU types (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, Apple Silicon, Ascend). Cloud Comfy Cloud Our official paid cloud version for those who can't afford local hardware. Examples See what ComfyUI can do with the newer template workflows or old example workflows . Features A visual node graph for building and reusing image, video, audio, 3D, and text workflows without code. Reusable subgraphs, workflow templates, App Mode, and a local API for integrating workflows into applications. Efficient local execution with asynchronous queueing, partial graph re-execution, smart VRAM and RAM management, model offloading, and support for quantized models. Broad native model support. This is a representative list; browse the workflow library for maintained, ready-to-run templates. Image generation : Stable Diffusion 1.5, SDXL, SD3.5, Flux.1, Flux.2, Qwen Image, Z-Image, Hunyuan Image 2.1, HiDream, Lumina Image 2.0, Chroma, Anima, LongCat Image, Ideogram 4, Krea 2, MageFlow, Microsoft Lens, PixelDiT, Kandinsky 5, and Ernie Image. Image editing : Flux Kontext, Flux.2 Klein, Qwen Image Edit, HiDream E1.1 and O1, OmniGen2, Boogu, JoyImage Edit, MageFlow Edit, and LongCat Image Edit. Video generation : Wan 2.1 and 2.2, LTX-Video 2 and 2.3, HunyuanVideo 1.5, Kandinsky 5 Video, CogVideoX, Cosmos Predict2, Bernini-R, SCAIL 2, and Mochi. Audio and video generation : MiniMax H3 and LTX-AV. Audio generation : ACE-Step 1.5, Stable Audio 3, MiniMax Music 3 and Yue 2. 3D and vision : Hunyuan3D 2.1, TripoSplat, SeedVR2, SUPIR, Depth Anything 3, MoGe, SAM 3 and 3.1, RT-DETRv4, and BiRefNet. Text generation : Gemma 3 and 4, Qwen3, Qwen3.5, and Qwen3-VL, including multimodal inputs. Load complete checkpoints or separate diffusion models, VAEs, text encoders, LoRAs, ControlNets, adapters, and upscalers from supported model formats. Built-in tools for inpainting, outpainting, reference conditioning, masks and compositing, model merging, upscaling, frame interpolation, segmentation, depth estimation, and media processing. Save and load workflows as JSON, or recover complete workflows and seeds from supported generated media. Runs fully offline: core does not download anything unless you request it. Use --offline to disable the optional paid Comfy API nodes and force all built-in functionality to stay offline, or --disable-partner-nodes to only disable the API nodes. Extend ComfyUI with custom nodes Configure additional model locations with extra_model_paths.yaml . Support for saving and loading high bit depth images and videos: 16 bit PNG images, 32 bit EXR, 10 bit AVIF are supported and more. Support for saving and loading HDR videos and images in various formats. Release Process ComfyUI follows a weekly release cycle targeting Monday but this regularly changes because of model releases or large changes to the codebase. There are three interconnected repositories: ComfyUI Core Releases a new major stable version (e.g., v0.7.0) roughly every 2 weeks. Starting from v0.4.0 patch versions will be used for fixes backported onto the current stable release. Minor versions will be used for releases off the master branch. Patch versions may still be used for releases on the master branch in cases where a backport would not make sense. Commits outside of the stable release tags may be very unstable and break many custom nodes. Serves as the foundation for the desktop release Comfy Desktop Builds a new release using the latest stable core version ComfyUI Frontend Every 2+ weeks frontend updates are merged into the core repository Features are frozen for the upcoming core release Development continues for the next release cycle Shortcuts Keybind Explanation Ctrl + Enter Queue up current graph for generation Ctrl + Shift + Enter Queue up current graph as first for generation Ctrl + Alt + Enter Cancel current generation Ctrl + Z / Ctrl + Y Undo/Redo Ctrl + S Save workflow Ctrl + O Load workflow Ctrl + A Select all nodes Alt + C Collapse/uncollapse selected nodes Ctrl + M Mute/unmute selected nodes Ctrl + B Bypass selected nodes (acts like the node was removed from the graph and the wires reconnected through) Delete / Backspace Delete selected nodes Ctrl + Backspace Delete the current graph Space Move the canvas around when held and moving the cursor Ctrl / Shift + Click Add clicked node to selection Ctrl + C / Ctrl + V Copy and paste selected nodes (without maintaining connections to outputs of unselected nodes) Ctrl + C / Ctrl + Shift + V Copy and paste selected nodes (maintaining connections from outputs of unselected nodes to inputs of pasted nodes) Shift + Drag Move multiple selected nodes at the same time Ctrl + D Load default graph Alt + + Canvas Zoom in Alt + - Canvas Zoom out Ctrl + Shift + LMB + Vertical drag Canvas Zoom in/out P Pin/Unpin selected nodes Ctrl + G Group selected nodes Q Toggle visibility of the queue H Toggle visibility of history R Refresh graph F Show/Hide menu . Fit view to selection (Whole graph when nothing is selected) Double-Click LMB Open node quick search palette Shift + Drag Move multiple wires at once Ctrl + Alt + LMB Disconnect all wires from clicked slot Ctrl can also be replaced with Cmd instead for macOS users Installing Windows and Mac We highly recommend using the desktop app : Link to Download The desktop app is the easiest and best way to use ComfyUI for new users. Windows Portable There is a portable standalone build for Windows that should work for running on Nvidia GPUs or for running on your CPU only. It is not recommended for regular users. Regular users should use the desktop app above. Direct link to download (nvidia) Simply download, extract with 7-Zip or with the windows explorer on recent windows versions and run. For smaller models you normally only need to put the checkpoints (the huge ckpt/safetensors files) in: ComfyUI\models\checkpoints but many of the larger models have multiple files. Make sure to follow the instructions to know which subfolder to put them in ComfyUI\models\ If you have trouble extracting it, right click the file -> properties -> unblock The portable above currently comes with python 3.13 and pytorch cuda 13.0. Update your Nvidia drivers if it doesn't start. All Official Portable Downloads: Portable for AMD GPUs Portable for Intel GPUs Portable for Nvidia GPUs (supports 20 series and above). Portable for Nvidia GPUs with pytorch cuda 12.6 and python 3.12 (Supports Nvidia 10 series and older GPUs, DO NOT USE THIS ON NEWER 20 SERIES AND ABOVE GPUS). How do I share models between another UI and ComfyUI? See the Config file to set the search paths for models. In the standalone windows build you can find this file in the ComfyUI directory. Rename this file to extra_model_paths.

Looking forward to building impactful projects with you! TradingAgents Framework TradingAgents is a multi-agent trading framework that mirrors the dynamics of real-world trading firms. By deploying specialized LLM-powered agents: from fundamental analysts, sentiment experts, and technical analysts, to trader, risk management team, the platform collaboratively evaluates market conditions and informs trading decisions. Moreover, these agents engage in dynamic discussions to pinpoint the optimal strategy. TradingAgents framework is designed for research purposes. Trading performance may vary based on many factors, including the chosen backbone language models, model temperature, trading periods, the quality of data, and other non-deterministic factors. It is not intended as financial, investment, or trading advice. Our framework decomposes complex trading tasks into specialized roles. Analyst Team Fundamentals Analyst: Evaluates company financials and performance metrics, identifying intrinsic values and potential red flags. Sentiment Analyst: Aggregates news headlines, StockTwits, and Reddit chatter into a single sentiment read to gauge short-term market mood. News Analyst: Monitors global news and macroeconomic indicators, interpreting the impact of events on market conditions. Technical Analyst: Utilizes technical indicators (like MACD and RSI) to detect trading patterns and forecast price movements. The selected analysts work at the same time, each on its own tools, and the research debate starts once all of their reports are in. Researcher Team Comprises both bullish and bearish researchers who critically assess the insights provided by the Analyst Team. Through structured debates, they balance potential gains against inherent risks. Trader Agent Composes reports from the analysts and researchers to make informed trading decisions, determining the timing and magnitude of trades. Risk Management and Portfolio Manager Continuously evaluates portfolio risk by assessing market volatility, liquidity, and other risk factors. The risk management team evaluates and adjusts trading strategies, providing assessment reports to the Portfolio Manager for final decision. The Portfolio Manager approves/rejects the transaction proposal. If approved, the order will be sent to the simulated exchange and executed. conda activate tradingagents Or with uv : uv venv --python 3.13 source .venv/bin/activate Install the package and its dependencies ( uv pip install . with uv): pip install . Docker Alternatively, run with Docker: cp .env.example .env # add your API keys docker compose run --rm tradingagents After updating the repository, rebuild the image with docker compose build . Results, reports, the memory log and the cache live in the tradingagents_data volume. To keep them in a folder on the host instead, create the folder and point TRADINGAGENTS_DATA_DIR at it, in .env or the shell: mkdir -p data && TRADINGAGENTS_DATA_DIR=./data docker compose run --rm tradingagents . For local models with Ollama: docker compose --profile ollama run --rm tradingagents-ollama Required APIs TradingAgents supports multiple LLM providers. ASPIRE: Agentic /Skills Discovery for Robotics Project Page | Paper ASPIRE is a new type of continual learning: "training" is skill refinement instead of gradient descent. read the iterative-debugging skill (.claude/skills/iterative-debugging/SKILL.md) and
